title: introduce profile-curator service and autoconfig economizer for workload defaults
author: Aisha Patel
commits: Initialize profile-curator microservice and HTTP API (cmd/curator)
Implement economizer engine: workload simulator, unit-econ scoring, profile candidate generator
Hook into controller: rollout plan, canary evaluator and safety fallthrough rules
Add CLI: curator apply/dry-run/score and operator docs
Integration tests and simple benchmark harness
description:
Motivation: Many customers and our own Dedicated clusters have operational drift between deployed inference defaults and the actual workload shapes. Engineers repeatedly tune batching, prefill TTLs, and quantization profiles per-model which leads to inconsistent unit economics and frequent regressions. This PR introduces a new Profile Curator service and an AutoConfig Economizer that can simulate workload slices, score candidate default profiles by unit-economic impact, and propose safe rollout plans.

What this change does: Adds a lightweight curator microservice (HTTP + internal gRPC proxy) that discovers model variants and recent telemetry, runs a candidate generation pipeline that emits batching/caching/quant profiles, simulates token-level cost/latency with a small stochastic workload sampler, and computes unit-econ deltas (cost per successful completion, tail latency impact). The output is: (1) a ranked set of profile candidates with expected savings and risk score, (2) a canary rollout plan that includes traffic split, fallthrough thresholds, and automatic rollback hooks.

Key features: 1) Profile generator: rule + ML hybrid that recommends batch_size, max_latency_target, kv_cache_ttl, quant_profile (int4/int8/config) per model family. 2) Unit-econ simulator: lightweight token-cost model using our serving runtime metrics to estimate GPU token cost, memory pressure, and expected tail-latency changes. 3) Safety and rollout: canary evaluator that monitors real-time observability hooks (error rate, P95, token drop) and enforces fallback to pinned profiles if thresholds are exceeded. 4) CLI and operator docs: curator apply/dry-run/score, and operator guide in docs/operations/cost-automation.md.

Backward compatibility and rollout strategy: The curator only creates suggested profiles and a rollout plan; it does not change runtime defaults until an operator approves and applies the plan (dry-run by default). We ship an optional operator mode to allow automatic application when a minimum expected savings threshold is exceeded and the canary passes. All generated profiles include an explicit safety tier and a default-to-pinned fallback.

Testing: Unit tests for the economizer engine and profile generator, integration tests that run a short simulated traffic replay against a local runtime stub, and a small perf harness to validate cold-start and KV-cache interactions. One flaky integration test (tests/integration/profile_curator_test.go) failed once on CI due to timing; it was retried and passed.

Related work: follows patterns from the optimizer workstream (ENG-7102) and complements the cost dashboards by producing actionable defaults instead of manual recommendations.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the economizer scoring math (internal/curator/autoconfig/economizer.go) and the safety evaluator thresholds in controller/rollout/curator_integration.go. The quantization selector is intentionally conservative (prefers int8 fallback profiles when int4 risk score > 0.15).
discussion: Samir Shah (reviewer): Can you explain how the unit-econ simulator handles bursty tail requests? Aisha Patel (author): The simulator samples from the recent inter-arrival distribution and includes a tail sampler that upweights high-latency sequences; results in a conservative P95 estimate. Samir Shah: Are the KV cache TTL recommendations per-model or global? Aisha Patel: Per-model by default with a global override flag for operator workflows. Lina Chen (reviewer): We need clearer metrics wiring for rollback hooks — can you add a.k.a. an observable contract? Aisha Patel: Added contract docs and placed hooks in controller/rollout; included tests that assert rollback on P95 > threshold. Evan Brooks (reviewer): The quant profile selection looks aggressive for small models. Consider minimum traffic floor before switching to int4. Aisha Patel: Good call — implemented a traffic floor of 100 reqs/min per-shard before proposing int4. Integrations team (comment): CI integration tests flaky under low resources — recommend running the bench harness on dedicated runners. Aisha Patel: Added a flag to skip heavy bench on shared CI and noted the runner requirement in docs. Final approval: Samir Shah approved, Lina Chen approved (with docs note), Evan Brooks approved.
merge_outcome: merged via squash (squash-merge) after CI green and approvals
release_notes: Add Profile Curator microservice and AutoConfig Economizer: generates safe batching/caching/quantization default profiles, simulates unit economics, and produces canary rollout plans. Operator approval required for automatic application. CLI: curator score/apply/dry-run. See docs/operations/cost-automation.md for operator guidance.
